lesson_title: One Pile In, One Pile Out
hook_text: A brand-new garden service has sixteen thousand rand in the bank after one month. So why did it earn only five hundred and forty-five rand?
clip_script: End of June. A mixed pile of papers. Ask each one a single question: money in, or money out? In goes to the cash receipts journal: the owner's fifteen thousand, a ten thousand rand bank loan, customers' fees, forty rand interest. Out goes to the cash payments journal: a lawnmower, wages, fuel, advertising, drawings, a loan repayment, bank charges. Add every column. In: thirty-one thousand and forty. Out: fourteen thousand seven hundred and ninety-five. Left in the bank: sixteen thousand two hundred and forty-five. But income was only six thousand and forty, expenses five thousand four hundred and ninety-five. Profit: five hundred and forty-five rand. The rest was borrowed or contributed.
visual_style: A whiteboard desk with a paper pile splitting into two stacks labelled in and out, two notebooks filling line by line, column totals ticking up, and a balance scale settling level.
mood: Brisk and tidy, with a surprising twist at the end.
pacing: Quick sorting montage, a steady totals count, then a slower reveal of the small profit.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and close off both journals yourself.
